utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Grujic. Just to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you very much. Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Grujic.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday during my cross-examination, we left off with the subject of expelled persons, and we showed on the ELMO one map of expelled persons broken down by counties. That is map number 6 in the addendum related to expelled persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher to put this map on the ELMO again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, we see now this map on the monitor or, rather, we see the territory of the Republic of Croatia with counties designated. And in addition to that, we have a table showing the number of expelled persons broken down by counties. We have viewed it -- reviewed it yesterday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how many counties do we see in Croatia on this map?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, can you tell us is this the total number of counties with county being the basic unit of territorial organisation in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What we see here are only the counties from which a certain number of expelled persons was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher to replace that map with this one. That is map number 3 related to Prosecution Exhibit called Martic Court Binder. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: This map shows the territory of the Yugoslav Republic of Croatia in 1991, divided into the then-existing municipalities. Are you familiar with this division into municipalities, Mr. Grujic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it was divided into municipalities, but I cannot confirm that it is exactly as shown on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: This map was developed by the Prosecution, and according to this under the territory of Croatia in 1991 there were about 110 municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the usher to show us map number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, this is the map of the Republic of Croatia showing the municipalities that were covered by the then-existing SAO Krajina as of end 1991, and red lines show the borders of the area controlled by the then SAO Krajina, later the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Do you see the municipalities that belong to the territory of the SAO Krajina as shown on this map?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I wonder if you can assist the Trial Chamber by telling us how many persons were expelled from the territory of these municipalities bordered by the red lines which were the SAO Krajina in 1991.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only repeat what I said the last time. I provided you with numbers that apply to the existing, current division into counties, and basically it covers these municipalities as well. Counties were partly occupied, and the people recorded as expelled were expelled solely from these occupied territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, does that mean that you cannot give us the number of expelled persons broken down by municipalities bordered by this red line that shows the territory of SAO Krajina, later RSK?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, I don't have numbers by municipalities. I have numbers by counties. But since these counties cover the same territory as the former municipalities, the numbers correspond. But the current prevailing division into counties is the basis of all the material I have produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Regarding the number of expellees, and you mention that in para 34a of your report, the number being 220.338 persons, with a breakdown by ethnicity, do you stand by that number, even broken down by ethnicity in your report?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly do. This data was gathered from people who were expelled. Each of them has their ID as an expellee. Their dossiers were formed, and on the basis of this information we have obtained the picture as I have presented it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: According to item 2 of an agreement between the Defence and the Prosecution, one of the stipulated facts is that according to the census of 1991, there were 3.736.353; Croats -- 12 per cent of Serbs, 106.461 Yugoslavs, and 244.381 persons who did not declare their ethnicity. That is 6.1 per cent. I didn't mention Muslims there. There were 0.5 per cent of Muslims. Are you familiar with these numbers?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the total number of the population in 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: According to this agreement between the Defence and the Prosecution, on the territory of Croatia there was a total of 4.784.265 citizens, out of which 581.663 Serbs, or 12 per cent. Do you know these numbers?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the numbers we have from the institute for statistics, that is the exact number of the population in 1991, and the breakdown by ethnicity as you mentioned. That is a general piece of information, not something specific to your agreement with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this agreement that I just mentioned, another stipulated fact is that this area was covered by UNPAs, United Nations Protected Areas, and that there existed three zones, Eastern Slavonia, Western Slavonia, and Krajina. These zones encompassed certain municipalities. Do you know that there were three zones?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not exactly as you specified them. I know that certain sectors existed that constituted UNPAs, but I don't know them as krajinas or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, maybe I wasn't clear enough. Do you know that on the territory of the Yugoslav Republic of Croatia certain UNPAs were established by decision of the United Nations Security Council, and there were three of them?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that, but that's not the subject of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Eastern Slavonia, as one of the zones, encompassed municipalities Beli Manastir? Can you show it on the map?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Parts of Osijek lying to the east of Osijek town.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality but not the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Part of the municipality to the east of the town.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Vukovar and certain villages in the farthest eastern part of Vinkovci. Can you show that on the map?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for Western Slavonia and Krajina, the municipalities covered by UNPAs were enumerated according to United Nations document as Grubisno Polje, Daruvar, Pakrac, Western parts of Nova Gradiska and eastern parts Novska. Do you see these areas on the map?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: As for Krajina as an UNPA, it encompassed the municipalities of Kostajnica, Petrinja, Dvor Na Uni, Glina, Vrginmost, Vojnic, Slunj, Titova Korenica, Donji Lopac, Gracac, Obrovac, Benkovac, and Knin. Are these bordered by the red line on the map?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic. In annex 3 of the amended indictment against Mr. Martic, the composition of the population in municipalities covered by this indictment is as follows regarding SAO Krajina: For Benkovac which had a total of 33.378 citizens, 13.353 Croats, 25 Muslims and 18.986 Serbs. The population of local communes near Zadar that annexed themselves to Benkovac had a total of 302 -- 500, 249 [as interpreted], out of which 1.992 Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't follow the other numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you will already that this is not the subject of my testimony, and I have not spoken about the ethnic composition of municipalities. I spoke about the ethnic composition of expelled persons by counties. And on this map I just confirmed to you those borders. Let me show you again on the map. It's very clear that those municipalities that you designated, Beli Manastir and eastern Osijek, that comes under the Osijek-Baranja county we spoke about. Vukovar and the eastern part of Vinkovci comes under the Vukovar-Srem county. So all these areas are parts of the counties for which I provided you with statistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, the interpreters said they didn't hear the rest of the numbers in your question. You talked about 302 to 549 or 500, 200, I don't know what we are saying there, and what is written there is "500, 249," which is not actually intended to be 500.249. I don't know what number it is you wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was talking about Benkovac, which was part of SAO Krajina as stated in the indictment. 5.294 was the total population of those municipalities that annexed themselves to Benkovac and that became part of Krajina. So it's 5.294, if that's the number you asked me about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Having asked you about that, this witness has repeatedly been saying to you that he didn't deal with these numbers by municipality, but he dealt with them by -- what did you say? What did you call them again? By counties. I'm just sitting here and trying to figure out where you're going with all this cross-examination, and I really don't see where you're going. He's told you again, and again and again, that he has not dealt with the census of the populations of the various places, that he has dealt with the numbers of the expellees from the various counties. What do you expect him to tell you? Just what do you want from him? Maybe we can understand what you want from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my next question, in order to understand why I put the previous question, was as follows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Don't tell us the next question. Tell us what you want from this witness. You'll ask the next question once we've understood where you're going and we allow you to ask the next question. I've been trying to hold myself to say the witness will deal with you and he has tried to deal with you as best he can, to tell you exactly what he knows and what he doesn't know, and what it is he has prepared for this Court. But I want to know what is it you want him to tell you so that maybe we can put the question to him and he can tell you. But if he doesn't have the answers, then he doesn't have the answers. What do you want from him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll tell you right away. In annex 3 of the indictment, there is a list of the municipalities making up the SAO Krajina, and these were Benkovac, Knin, Obrovac, Gracac, Donji Lapac, Korenica, Slunj, Vrginmost, Glina, Dvor Na Uni, Kostajnica, Petrinja. These were the municipalities individually listed in annex 3 of the amended indictment along with a number of inhabitants in each of these municipalities. On page 4 of this annex, and this is the essence of my question, it says that the overall population of the SAO Krajina in 1991 was 286.716. Of these, there were 78.611 Croats, 1.932 Muslims, and 193.649 Serbs. Therefore, according to the amended indictment, there were 78.611 Croats living there, whereas the expert insists that the number of Croats expelled was 209.000 plus an additional 220.000 people, which means that more than half of the people who were expelled were Serbs. So I would like to know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Why don't you just put that to him? How is it possible that 220.000 Croats are expelled when the total population was 78.000? You do that in one sentence, not in ten pages. You just put that to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, your opposite number is on her feet. Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Pardon me. I think my opposite number has listed the municipalities in the SAO Krajina from the annex in the indictment. However, my opposite number has failed to address certain areas such as Vukovar, Srem, Osijek, Baranja, Sisak, Moslavina, which are represented in the charts presented by the witness. These have been omitted from what Mr. Milovancevic presents in his total population figures. I just wish to point that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Valabhji. May I just add, Mr. Milovancevic, that in fact what I see you doing is you are arguing with the witness. What you are -- you're not cross-examining the witness. What you are doing is what you should be doing in argument at the end of the trial. If your case is that the total number of Croats was -- in the whole of the SAO Krajina was 78.000, just tell him. Tell him that it is impossible to have 220.000 Croats being expelled because that is far in excess of the number of the Croats that existed -- that lived in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I may have been going there in and roundabout way, and this is due to misunderstandings about the territorial division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is a very roundabout way, and your cross-examination, let me tell you, Mr. Milovancevic, is very roundabout, you know. You're really not getting to the points that you need to get to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, according to the indictment against Mr. Martic from which he is defending himself, in annex 3 the total population of the SAO Krajina in 1991 was 286.716 persons. Of that, 78.611 were Croats, 1.932 were Muslims --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have told us that. Just carry on, please. You have told us all that. No, no, no. You have told the witness that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you explain the fact that the number of expellees in your report who are of Croat ethnicity is 3 times bigger than the total number of Croats inhabiting the territory covered by this indictment?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not provide demographic information about the population figures. I doubt there is any mistake in the information I have provided. I doubt that it's possible, because there is a file number for each and every expellee I have counted, with their first and last name, other details, and the place from which they were expelled. Therefore, I have provided official information from the Bureau for Expellees, and I have to say that this information has been public and there have never been any objections to it. Also, that it corresponds to the information of the UNHCR. I have not, however, testified about the demographic situation in the Republic of Croatia. That is not the subject of my expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, the Prosecution claims that often the territory covered by the indictment, which is now on the map, and I have given you the population figures, that non-Serbs were expelled. The Prosecution has broken down the population by municipality, which is why I put those numbers to you. I'm asking you now how what you say is possible if in 1991, at the time of the conflict, according to the allegations of the Prosecution and according to the census of 1991, there were 78.611 Croats? Can you explain how it came about that 202.000 Croats were expelled from the area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, the question has been asked and answered. Can you ask the next question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When you were speaking about the number of expellees, you also mentioned 250 to 300.000 persons expelled according to estimates in 1995 during Operations Flash and Storm. You did not put them into the category of expellees. Are you aware of the fact that in that period during Operation Storm and after Operation Storm, according to the information of the UN, 22.000 homes of Serbs were destroyed by the end of October? And can you tell us what the status of those persons is, the persons who fled from the area in order to save their own lives, people whose homes have been razed to the ground, who cannot come back and yet you do not count them as the expellees?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two kinds of status, the status of an expellee and the status after refugee. I do not want to enter into a discussion but, but I have to say that is a big difference between the expellees from Vukovar. If you looked at the images, the videos, you saw them being expelled, escorted by armed men. They were threatened by weapons -- with weapons. They were also made to abandon their property in writing, signing documents. They were expelled at gunpoint. When we are discussing Operation Storm, you will allow for the fact that these people left in an organised manner, in columns. The Red Cross and other humanitarian services made it possible for them to receive food and drinks. They wanted to leave the area, and you will allow that the president of the republic and the government broadcast public announcements calling upon these people to remain in their homes. This population are defined as refugees. Not by me but by others, and this is a status that is recognised worldwide. Refugees are people who have crossed an international border and gone to a different country. These people have the status of refugees. These people are able to come back and, as I have said, 120.000 have already returned. The return is under way. There are 12.000 new applications for return which have been approved. Let me also to remind you, and I told you I don't want to enter into discussions with you which are not the subject of my testimony, but now that you ask me that, let me tell you that, yes, certainly there were many houses that were destroyed in those operations. Criminal actions have been tried within the Republic of Croatia, and these houses are now being restored. The government of the Republic of Croatia has a programme for the rebuilding of all houses destroyed, and these people are now returning. They have the status of returnees, and they are coming back to their homes. But that, again, is not the subject of my expert testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We are now talking about whether all expellees are included in your report. According to official Croatian information, do you know that in Operation Storm, for example, it ended officially between the 4th and 7th of August, 1995, whereas 22.000 houses were destroyed after that period, by the end of October? You say that new houses are being built for those people now, and you say that between 250 and 300.000 people left and that a certain number have returned. But for 11 years these refugees did not go back. Far fewer have come back than left, and the people who are coming back are facing enormous problems. Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what you expect me to say. If you want to enter into a discussion with me, we can have a very broad discussion, but I did not testify about this, and it is not the topic of my expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic. Are you aware of the fact that the Secretary-General of the UN presented to the General Assembly, on the 15th of May, 1993, information showing that on the territory of the Republic of Croatia, outside the territory of the SAO Krajina and outside the area of armed conflicts, from territories under the control of the Croatian government 251.000 Serbs were expelled? Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about this information. According to my information, about 30.000 people changed their place of residence within the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Milovancevic, are you still going to use the map that's on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Thank you, Your Honours. The map can be removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In connection with the number of expellees you mention in point 34a of your report, are you aware of the fact that the Presidency of Yugoslavia, on the 10th of April, 1992, sent a memorandum to Mr. Boutros Boutros-Ghali the Secretary-General of the UN pointing out that only in 1991, on the territory of Western Slavonia, 282 citizens of Serb ethnicity were killed, that many villages were destroyed, and that about 70.000 people were forced to leave their homes because of military operations by Croatian armed forces? Are you aware of this information?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, again, is not the subject of my testimony. I am here to testify about official records, not about certain political events. I am speaking of the official records kept by my office and the job that I'm doing, also about information that I received through official channels that have to do with my job. I put forward this information during my testimony, and I abide by it. As for your questions referring to certain political events, I really cannot testify about those. They are not the subject of my expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I am not referring to political events, Witness. I am simply trying to check the validity of the official information that you are presenting to the Trial Chamber. Prosecution witness Mr. Dzakula who testified in these proceedings, when answering to questions in cross-examination confirmed that in 1991 on the territory of Western Slavonia, according to information from April 1992, 129 villages were burnt, burnt down. 4.118 houses were destroyed, and all the population was expelled from those villages and houses. Do you have this information? Because these people are not on your list of expellees.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not absolutely sure that they don't exist. But when you ask a question like that, you should come up with names and surnames and ask to compare my lists with yours. I cannot tell you who was expelled by name and from which area. I have numbers about people who were expelled from a certain area, accompanied by statistics that are normally shown. And if you allow me just one more comment. Each person who came to the office for expelled persons, regardless of ethnicity, religion or whatever, was recorded as an expelled person. After that, they were put up in specialised camps or settlements or appropriate accommodation until the moment when they were able to return to their homes. All of those people, and they are, as I said, 220.338. And it's possible that they are recorded among those I have recorded by county. But if you want to compare my data with yours, I'll be happy to provide it. Our work is completely transparent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you didn't give me lists with names and surnames, so I didn't produce any myself, but you said in report that a number of expelled Serbs, in paragraph 34a, is 3 -- 3.104. Witness Dzakula, however, testified that only from Eastern Slavonia 70.000 people were expelled. But you have already answered my question, so I'll move on to another one. The Crisis Staff of Slavonska Pozega municipality announced on the 29th October, 1991, an order to evacuate all the citizens, all the residents of 24 villages, and item 2 orders the populous to go to other places in Slavonska Pozega municipality because of oncoming operations, and the residents are told to take only personal effects, valuables and money. According to the testimony of Witness Dzakula, those people were driven out and the villages burned. Do you have information about that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It doesn't fall within the scope of my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: What I want to know, and I would appreciate an answer, is how is it possible for the list of expelled persons from this territory to include 3.104 Serbs only when a wealth of other evidence is completely different?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, this is official data. It's transparent, and I produced it as such. You are trying to impose something on me all the time, and you neglect what I said earlier, that in addition to this number there was -- there were 7.000 others who did not specify their ethnicity, and there can be many Serbs among them. You stick to your numbers, and you completely disregard the other number that I mentioned in my testimony. You correctly quoted me as saying that there were 3.100 or so Serbs among the expelled, but there are also 7.032 others who did not state their ethnicity, including certainly Serbs. But I recorded them only as people who did not state their ethnicity. I couldn't do otherwise. But I certainly admit that they include Serbs as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is the purpose of my question. Can these 7.000 accommodate the 70.000 others who have not been mentioned at all? But let us move to imprisoned persons. That is paragraph 29 of your report, and we'll look at chart number 10. When you speak about imprisoned persons - that is paragraph 39, rather - do you mean only those who were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7.666 persons are on record as having been detained in camps and prisons on the territory of the occupied Republic of Croatia, in the territory of Serbia and Montenegro, which was then FRY, and the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it can be said that these formed a single, unified system of camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you keep referring to the occupied territory of Croatia, to avoid all misunderstanding I will put to you one fact that is stipulated between us and the Prosecution, and it is mentioned in 31(a) of the agreement on stipulated the facts and it says on 21st of February, 1992, this UN Security Council adopted Resolution 743 proclaiming a peace operation of the United Nations in certain areas in Croatia designated as United Nations Protected Areas. Furthermore, in this text, it is stated that UNPAs shall be established in areas where Serbs form a majority or a significant minority and where intra-communal tensions have led to conflict in recent past. Do you know that UNPAs were set up precisely in those areas where Serbs formed a majority or a significant minority?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already answered this question. I told you that I know that UNPAs were established under the aegis of the United Nations, but I also said that those areas were and still are parts of the territory of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the amended indictment, we see that the number of Serbs in these areas is 268.000 in total -- sorry. The total population of these areas is 268.000, out of which 78.000 Croats. The rest were Serbs. Are you telling me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it 268 or 286?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: May I while my opposite number is searching for some material?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I see that he has equated the population of 286.000, which he probably made a mistake and 268.000, inversed the numbers. In the indictment he's equated the figure with UNPAs whereas that figure pertains to the SAO Krajina. I think I mentioned this before. So I would really advise my learned counsel to double-check before he presents his questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Valabhji. You hear that, Mr. Milovancevic. Any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: So the gist of my question was this: According to the indictment, the total population of SAO Krajina was 286.000. 78.611 were Croats and the rest were Serbs. Is Mr. Grujic claiming that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have put this question so many times, and I've asked you at some stage that when you have put the question, get on to the next question. What do you want this witness to say, Mr. Milovancevic? He's not dealing with the statistics of the SAO Krajina. He's dealing with the people who have been reported to him as either dead, expelled, deported, displaced. What do you want this witness to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Prosecution does not use the term "occupied areas." United Nations referred to United Nations protected areas. It is the witness who uses the term "occupied areas." I want him to tell us why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Because that's where he worked from his office. He worked with occupied areas. He doesn't work with UNPAs. You can't force him to use your terminology. What you have agreed with the Prosecution is the agreement with the Prosecution. You have to extrapolate that he told you from what is relevant to your case. Do you want him to go back to the drawing-board and then start drawing his papers using the term SAO Krajina instead of occupied areas? He surely can't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And please let's get on with the case, Mr. Milovancevic. You have been really going in circles around the same issue, you know, this whole question of numbers, which I don't think anybody else understands in this court except yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, in paragraph 39 we have a list of detained persons. Is your office the source of this information?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my office is the source of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 88 per cent are males according to this information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to have a look. 88 per cent are men, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that 89 per cent out of those whose age is known is between 18 and 60?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: But you say that for 1.789 persons detained the age was unknown.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: How come this number is so high?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In every previous chapter we've discussed, expelled persons and so on - we are now talking about camps - I provided you with the data that is available to me, and on several occasions I explained, but I have to repeat, obviously, that statistics are compiled based on available data. In all those cases when details incomplete and could be misleading, the case is placed in the category "Unknown." Either the person did not state their year of birth, or in other cases they did not state their ethnicity, or for some administrative reason this detail was not recorded. But very clearly we have a certain number of detained persons with a specified age and a certain number of people whose age has not been stated. We saw on previous examples that this is a statistically valid picture, because 75 per cent of it is properly recorded information, complete information, and provides a representative picture. I don't know if I was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I ask you this question for a particular reason. If we talk about dead who were exhumed and it is impossible to determine their age by post-mortem, I understand, but if we are dealing with living persons, I didn't -- I wasn't able to understand how come their age is unknown, but you've just explained. You also say that for 47 per cent of the detained it is not determined, it is not known, whether they were civilians or members of armed force.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we don't have that detail. We don't have that information, and we categorise them as unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Out of those whose status is known, 52 per cent are classified as -- as defenders, 2.094 members of armed forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In your report, you state that the ethnicity of as many as 1.878 detained persons is unknown?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why this number is so high?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As in the previous statistics, let me repeat. A person does not have to tell us what their ethnic affiliation is. Those who wanted to provide this information provided it. Those who didn't want to didn't, and they were classified as persons of unknown ethnicity. According to all international standards, you cannot coerce a person into telling you what their ethnic affiliation or their religion is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, you did give this answer yesterday, didn't you, several times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when speaking about the statistics, in every chapter about which counsel has asked me questions, I stated very clearly that -- where information was unknown I stated that it was unknown for the sake of clarity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And all I'm saying is you did give this answer yesterday several times and today, too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'll ask you to ask new questions, Mr. Milovancevic, otherwise I'm going to have to stop you each time you a question that has already been asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In your report referring to length of detention, you say that as many as 2.052 persons is not known for how long they were detain. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why this number is so high?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to explain. Some people were captured -- or, rather, these people were captured, and when they left, when they were exchanged, and you will allow that their experience was very difficult, I won't go into that, they could not recall the date. And you will allow that it's quite normal and human that they couldn't remember the date of their capture, whether it was the 13th or the 15th. In order to have precise information, we had to put these people into the category of unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: According to your report, out of the persons for whom it is known how long they were detained, 72 per cent were imprisoned between 30 days and one year. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: This seems a very long time. Do you have -- or, rather, the span is too long. The range is too long. Do you have precise information as to how many were imprisoned for 30 days, six months, and so on?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were statistics relevant for the provision of psychosocial assistance. If necessary, of course we can go back and do this kind of analysis that you're asking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what time period and what territory this information about imprisoned persons refers to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first imprisonments began in July 1991, and as I said, the last prisoner was release the in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to the information in graph 10, these persons were imprisoned on the territory of Serbia, Montenegro, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and, as you say, the occupied territories of the Republic of Croatia. Is this in your report?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: According to your information, a total of 2.044 persons were imprisoned in these areas. As these proceedings relate to the SAO Krajina, do you have information referring to the SAO Krajina or the municipalities which it comprised?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's provided in table 9, which clearly states that 2.404 persons were imprisoned in the previously occupied areas of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 38 of your report, you talk about the reliability of the information gathered on persons in detention, and there you say that most of those persons were registered by the International Committee of the Red Cross. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Information is provided as to the number of persons registered in detention by the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you give us an exhibit number of this graph that you're talking about, Mr. Milovancevic, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise for not having done that previously. This is the analysis of the information on persons detained, and I believe that this is Exhibit 298. If my learned friend can assist me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: It's ERN 04693033, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you please switch off your microphone while you're flipping paper, Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour. It's Exhibit 300.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit 300 it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, in graph 10, which you prepared, it says that 2.404 persons were imprisoned in the occupied territories of the Republic of Croatia and that the ICRC confirmed only 499 of these, whereas they did not confirm 1.905 of them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We will now move on to document number 11, and these are statistics by settlement, referring to Bacin, Dubica, Cerovljani, and Nadin. My first question in connection with these statistics referring to these villages is as follows: You provide information on the population in 1991, and as your source you mentioned the state bureau of statistics and other statistics. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your other sources are?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Information received from the present-day municipalities and villages mentioned, the literature about those places, and I can list what that is, but the basis is the bureau of statistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You have just said that the information also comes from the municipalities in which these villages are located. However, you say that you mention -- you say that you only used information from counties.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the present-day counties there are also municipalities. For example, the municipality of Hrvatska Dubica which is part of the Sisak-Moslavina county where these two villages are, Bacin and Cerovljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: So this municipality existed then and it exists today and it's part of this county. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hrvatska Dubica did exist. I don't know whether it was a municipality in 1991 or not, but it's a municipality now. And as I was now working on this information, I used the information from that municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that for some categories in your report you did use information from municipalities and not for others. In the case ever expellees or detainees you didn't and now you did.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you will allow me the right to use my sources and check my sources when drawing up my expert report. I'm allowed to use different sources and different kind of literature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In connection with Bacin, Dubica, Cerovljani, Nadin, you say the number killed was unknown. Is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We don't have the precise number of those who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In connection with the villages where it's stated that there are those who were killed, I'm referring to Skabrnja, Bruska, Saborsko, Lipovaca, and Poljane, the status of those who were killed is mentioned for only one of those places. That is whether they were soldiers, civilians, or members of the civilian protection; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check, but let me repeat. I have provided the information I had. I cannot provide information where I don't have it. You can ask me about the information I have provided. You can ask me whether it's correct or not. You cannot ask me that about information I don't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: As this information is provided only in the case of Lipovaca, does your reply mean that you didn't have in information for the other places?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. If I didn't have information, I didn't provide it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: With respect to Nadin, according to the information you provide, the number of expellees is larger than the number of inhabitants. You speak of 699 expellees, whereas Nadin had 666 inhabitants in total. How do you explain this?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evidently there has been a permutation between the population and the expellees. 699 should be the number of inhabitants, and 666 should be the number of expellees. So there has been a permutation of figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When referring to Bacin, and that's document number 12, its ERN is 0649-3262-0469-3264, the document about Bacin represents a list of 108 persons from Bacin, Dubica, and Cerovljani. According to paragraph 26 of the indictment these people were killed. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How many did you say? Would you be kind enough to repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, on the last page of this list it says that there are 108 persons on the list. You can check that.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The list includes 108 names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Just before the break, let me put another brief question. You compared this with your information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Your Honours, this is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Court adjourned, and will come back at quarter to eleven. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting. I see you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. If I might just take a moment of the Court's time to -- with regard to a scheduling matter, and I raise it now because it may require certain preparations be made today. As the Court is aware, we have two witnesses remaining for this week. The next witness, Mr. Strinovic, is making his second appearance at the Tribunal because he was here ready to testify during the week that was cancelled after -- because of the illness of Mr. Martic. So he's here for a second time ready to testify. The third witness, who is a short witness -- oh, actually, if I -- I'm sorry, Your Honour. If I -- before I make reference to this if we could move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May -- before we forget then, we will sit in Courtroom I tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, before the break we left off with a list of victims in Bacin. That is related to paragraph 26. That's from October 1991. Did we agree that according to this list there are 108 persons on this list? That was my last question before the break.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You compared this list to your information, and that is accurate.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I see from the document that out of those 108, 48 were exhumed and identified. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 48 persons were identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, only 48 of them have been confirmed as dead.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Among them is Ana Tepic, of Serb ethnicity, as we can see from the documentation of your office, 60R, Exhibit 373. Do you remember this detail?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ana Tepic is on the list, but I don't see the ethnicity at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 25 persons, according to the official records of your office, are registered as missing.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Are they still being sought?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those are people about whom we have no information whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: From this list of 108 persons recorded as victims in Bacin, you say that we have no information about 26 persons or they are absent from all of your records.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that nobody reported them as missing?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that nobody reported their disappearance, which is an evermore frequent occurrence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that those 26 persons are not even on the list of those 12.078 persons we have mentioned?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't turn on my microphone. We'll move on to a document related to Vukovici village. You say that two persons were exhumed from individual graves and that four are registered as dead?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Milovancevic. Could you tell us to which exhibit you are referring, exhibit in terms of the admitted evidence, so then we could follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, document 12 in B/C/S. It's ERN 0469-3266.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think all this information is contained in Exhibit 301.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, did you process the list of 210 persons from Vukovici registered as victims?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it's contained in the annex.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You say that 96 were exhumed -- sorry, two persons were exhumed from individual graves, and four are registered as dead.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: One person is still on record as missing.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Concerning this list of 210 people from Vukovici, you have no information about three of them.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are not in any of the official records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I wonder if I'm on the same page here as my learned colleague. 210 people? The English translation we have is 210, and if I'm looking at the page from this exhibit pertaining to victims in Vukovici, I don't have a list of 210.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It must be the interpreter's error. We misheard, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can I assist? I'm talking about victims in Vukovici. That's list linked to paragraph 29, 7th November 1991, and there are 10 persons on it. And if I understood Mr. Grujic correctly, he confirmed that there are 10 persons. It's obviously a misinterpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said, Mr. Grujic, that you have no information whatsoever about three persons from that list. Does that mean that those three persons are also absent from the list of dead?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means they are not on the list of dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you speak about information regarding Nadin, that's document 04693269, the first case is Brus and Bruska, and Skabrnja, did your commission deal with these persons from Nadin, Skabrnja, and Bruska?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you specify what you mean when you say "deal with"? It is said in the document that we performed exhumations and identifications, so we were directly involved. Where it is stated that a certain victim is on the list of dead, we were involved administratively. So we did deal with all these persons in the way I have described throughout, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you one more brief question to make it completely clear. The information about these victims, Nadin, in the first case, and Skabrnja, did you receive this from other agencies?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that was my meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about the number of expellees from Lipovaca, you stated that accord together list of population from 1991, the total number was 267, and expellees were 210. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Lipovaca, according to the state institute for statistics, had a population of 267, and 210 were expelled as registered by the office for expellees and refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this information is contained in the collective exhibit 301.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, you talk about 210 expelled persons from Lipovaca, (redacted) that before the arrival of the JNA at the village in end September or early October, the locals left the village and only 15 elderly persons remained. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they probably waited -- if they had waited for the armed forces to arrive, they would probably now be in a different category, not in the category of the expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You refer to them as expelled, but another witness says that they had left the village a day earlier. Does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. I'm telling you that 210 people are registered by the office for expellees, and they were accommodated as expellees in appropriate camps, and they had the status of expelled persons in Croatia until they returned to their homes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a send, Mr. Milovancevic. That name -- the name that you referred to of that witness, is it not a protected witness? Is that witness - I don't want to repeat the name a second time - on line -- page 35, line 12, was that not a protected witness? Shouldn't we delete that name?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you are right. I made a mistake inadvertently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Can we delete that name, please. Thank you very much. You may proceed. Were you rising on the same issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it was the same issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When you talk about the number of expellees from Cerovljani, you say that the population according to the census of 1991 was 512, and expellees were 203. Is that correct, Mr. Grujic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me check. Yes. Would you please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about Cerovljani. It is stated at the top of the report that according to the census of 1991 there were 512 residents and 203 were expelled. Is that in your report?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Two Prosecution witnesses who appeared earlier in the proceedings testified that Tomislav Mateljak, head of the Crisis Staff of Hrvatska Dubica ordered the evacuation of residents of Hrvatska Dubica and surrounding villages. Another witness who is from Hrvatska Dubica itself also spoke about the evacuation of the population from Hrvatska Dubica and the surrounding villages before the 14th of September, before those villages were captured, occupied. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not going into the circumstances under which somebody left their home. I have information, and I stand by it, that those people are categorised as expellees, and I don't want to go into the way in which they left their homes. That is not the subject of my testimony. I'm telling you about official records, and each person listed in those records has a file behind them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was the thrust of my question. When you talk about expellees from Cerovljani, do you dispose of information that the Crisis Staff of Cerovljani, Dubica, and Nadin had ordered an evacuation of the population?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have that at my disposal nor am I supposed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic. The next point I wanted to raise with you relates to events concerning Zagreb, document number 12. The last digits of the document number in B/C/S is 3274. That's Exhibit 303. On the list of dead in Zagreb on the 2nd and 3rd of May, 1995, which is appended to the indictment there are seven persons. However, according to your records five persons were killed and there is no information about two of those people. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information I have about the persons who were killed, five persons were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: This then does not include Ivan Brodac and Luka Skracic who are on this list of seven persons; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have to check that. There are two persons about whom I do not have information, which doesn't mean that this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Your office deals with prisoners and missing persons. Do those killed in Zagreb come under your purview?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course they do. Their mortal remains were examined in the Institute for Forensic Medicine, and this information has been included in the information on persons who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, when responding to my questions, you said that in Operations Flash and Storm between 250 and 300.000 persons fled. You said most of them were of Serb ethnicity. Can you tell us the number of persons who fled during Operation Flash from Western Slavonia in May 1995?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that these were estimates, estimates coming from various sources. This is not official information. This is just information I have, and it is an overall number. I cannot provide information about particular areas or municipalities. I can only speak about returnees who are registered as such because I have precise information about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You say you can speak about returnees. Is that something your office deals with? Because you are the Office for Expellees and Missing Persons.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But let me explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than once during your examination I stated very clearly why this information is kept in my office although it is not listed in the decree. I said that the administration of which I am the head also negotiates with the Commission for Humanitarian Issues and Missing Persons from Serbia and Montenegro. It is for this reason, as the leader of the delegation, that I must have information about all the issues raised during such negotiations. Therefore, this information is delivered to me in an official capacity for the purposes of my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what number of persons were killed during Operation Flash in Western Slavonia? You spoke about the number of victims in Zagreb. Do you know about the number of victims on the territory of Western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information at the disposal of my office and falling within its purview, 168 persons were killed whose remains were found and buried in cemeteries. As I said, the international community and the representatives of Serbia and Montenegro were informed about this. The documentation for preliminary identification was delivered to them in the case for all persons for whom we had such documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly: These were persons whose remains were found and who were killed during Operation Flash?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have another question for you. Do you know something about the victims from Paulin Dvor village near Osijek who were transferred in containers or barrels to the area of Gospic where they were exhumed in 1997, and are these victims included in the list of victims you have presented?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of this case. This case was tried before the national court. It was my administration that carried out the exhumation together with the representatives of the International Criminal Tribunal. Some of these victims have already and identified. The others are still in the process of are identified. I cannot tell you if they are included in the updated list of those killed. If you were to give me the names, I would be able to check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Let's just check that we're talking about same case. I am speaking about 19 Serbs who were killed in a house in November 1991 and who in 1997 were transferred from one place under the control of the Croatian authorities to another territory under Croatian control, Gospic. Is that the case that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The International Criminal Tribunal entrusted me with organising the exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence has finished its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. Any re-examination, Ms. Valabhji?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Nothing from the Prosecution. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, may I ask you about the exhumations in general terms. With what forensic experts have you been cooperating?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the exhumation and identification, which are closely linked, we cooperate with experts of forensic medicine from various areas. There are forensic experts, and the whole process involves dentists, forensic technicians, anthropologists, X-ray specialists, a whole spectrum of forensic experts. Experts for DNA analysis are also involved in the process. All the various segments of forensic science are involved in the process of identification. On the location, the site of the exhumation, there are forensic experts who work there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: To what extent were international experts involved?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have had several different situations. There have been situations where we have been assisted by forensic experts, for example, from the Smithson [as interpreted] Institute in the USA. We have also cooperated with experts of the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can you repeat the name of the institute in the USA?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Smithson -- the Smithsonian institute. They were the ones who gave us our first information as we had no experience. That was the beginning of our work with their assistance. We have had contacts with the forensic department of the human rights organisation that did exhumations at Ovcara. We were there as monitors. We have also had relationships with experts coming from the ICTY. There were situations where we were the monitors, but it was ICTY experts who were in charge of the whole procedure. We have also had situations where we worked jointly on projects, and there have been situations where we were in charge of the exhumation and ICTY experts were observers. Of course, different kinds of experts were involved, the geologists, anthropologists, forensic scientists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: What was the role of this expert of the European Union which was to be seen in the video yesterday?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Republic of Croatia, the standpoint was that everything that had to do with exchanges of prisoners of war, exhumations of mass graves and individual graves, all these issues had to be fully transparent. That is why we issued invitations and still issue invitations to international organisations dealing with such issues. The gentleman who observed the process in Bacin was part of the European Community Monitoring Mission which was active on the territory of the Republic of Croatia. They were always informed of our activities and involved as monitors. We still deliver information about our activities to the OSCE, to the ICTY, and to the International Commission for Missing Persons. They participate as international monitors. We are also transparent for representatives of Serbia and Montenegro in case they are interested in any of our projects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now go back to this issue of the expellees, the figures where the Defence counsel, Mr. Milovancevic, suggested there was some clear discrepancy between your figure of over 220.000, expellees and the figure mentioned in the amended indictment in annex 3, which is 78.000? Can you help us to clarify that in the following terms: Do you know in which of the counties which you mentioned in your tables these municipalities mentioned in annex 3 of the amended indictment are located, to which counties these municipalities, the following municipalities are related? May I cite from annex 3 of the amended indictment? It gives an overall figure of 78.611 Croats as part of the population in SAO Krajina, and it is divided into 13 municipalities. Can you maybe help us to -- to show to which regions they are related? There is Benkovac, Knin, Obrovac, the first three. And you did, in your tables these -- this computer document concerning -- in English it says "displaced persons," but we clarified that it should be expelled persons. Document Exhibit number 299. You had these -- you had this -- can you -- on page 6 you have a map with -- of all Croatia and with red figures which are then summarised in the table on the right hand, starting with Vukovarska-Srijemska, 55.644. Do you see that? This is page 6.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Could you clarify what is mentioned in the annex 3 of the indictment contains the following municipalities, and you can maybe tell us to which of these counties these would relate. So it was first Benkovac, Knin, and Obrovac, these three.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Benkovac, Knin, and Obrovac are at present, I believe, in the Zadar county. I'm not absolutely sure about Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay. But Zadar county or near to that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's in Zadar county.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Then it's Gracac -- or Gracac, Donji Lapac, these two.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gracac is either in or on the border of the Zadar county, whereas Lapac might be in the Lika-Sinj county. It's very difficult for me to say but I believe that's how it is.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lika-Sinj. I understand. Then Korenica -- or Titova Korenica. You will allow me to correct myself. Knin belongs to the Sibenik-Knin county.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes. Sibensko-Kninska. Korenica, where is that today?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Korenica should be in the Lika-Sinj, Licko-Senjska county.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Slunj.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slunj ought to be in Karlovac county or on the border of the Lika-Sinj county. I do believe, though, that it's in Karlovac county.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Vojnic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also believe it's in Karlovac county.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Vrginmost?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that it's in Karlovac or maybe partly in the Lika-Sinj county. I couldn't say precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Glina?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Glina is in the Sisak-Moslavina county.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And then we have three left. This is Dvor Na Uni; Kostajnica, Hrvatska Kostajnica; and Petrinja. First Dvor Na Uni.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sisak-moss what convenient and county.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Kostajnica?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kostajnica is also in the Sisak-Moslavina county.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And Petrinja?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petrinja, also the Sisak-Moslavina county.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I think this kind of comparison was needed and was what the Defence counsel was asking for to have a picture, both in terms of the municipalities from 1991 and in the county structure of today. Thank you very much for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope that I have managed to explain. We have dealt with only a part of the counties in occupied Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, I'd like to find out from you, and it may seem overly simplistic, but what circumstances or what conditions had to apply for a person to be designated a missing person?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the criteria we use to record missing persons and which are almost identical to the criteria of the ICRC when registering missing persons, the family reports that a person has gone missing. The family has no information about that person. Subsequently, we check whether the family has received any kind of information through various mechanisms. The fundamental criterion is that the family has no knowledge about the family member and that they report this, that they give a statement, fill in a questionnaire, and sign as people searching for someone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Did the missing person have to be missing for any particular period, a stipulated period before the designation was attached?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in our case, but there is in the case of the ICRC, which is why we are constantly comparing our lists and updating our records between our office, the Croatian Red Cross, and the ICRC. These are control mechanisms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. ICRC? Please tell me. I'm sorry, I want to know what it means.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The International Committee of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, concerning, for example, the data analyses of persons killed, where these statistics referred to men and women, would those statistics include children, or would there be a separate category for children? I don't really see a separate category on any of the graphs or data.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not analyse the information in this way. There are several different criteria. Sometimes a person under the age of 14, sometimes a person under 16, and sometimes a person under 18 is considered a child. That is why we did not go into this kind of analysis, because there's no clear-cut criterion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: So children would be included in those figures or not? That's what I was trying to get from you.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They are included in those figures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to turn to Exhibit 318, and the first clip. If you recall, you were present and something was removed from the ground, a small green object which was looking rather like a vegetable to me, and it was picked up and wiped off. Can you say what that was? If you cast your mind back for me, please, to that first clip, Exhibit 318. I believe it was by a grave site.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that now. It was a hand grenade which was found when searching the terrain and attempting to establish a mass grave site. The hand grenade was found in the broader area of the mass grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm now going to move on to the third clip. About ten metres from the grave site cartridges were found. I just wanted to know if you were able to say what type of cartridges those were.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, there were cartridges belonging to several groups. To the best of my recollection, these were from automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: And the next question is could you say whether these cartridges were found, although 10 metres away, were they scattered or were they in one area?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in more than one area. They were concentrated on a surface of several square metres, five, six, up to 10 square metres in several clusters. There were three or four such clusters, to the best of my recollection. They were found in clusters, and they were marked as such, and you can see that on the footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Who marked them?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were marked by the criminal police following orders from the investigating court that was in charge of the investigation there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm going to ask you about the handling of your report, and Defence counsel, Mr. Milovancevic, has touched on this in his cross-examination, but I want to ask this question directly and pointedly. Did the source of your information and data affect in any way how you handled the data professionally in producing your final results?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Generally speaking, my position is that the professional attitude comes first and is subject to no influence.
